stories.title: OpenAI Withdraws Three Math Papers Due to Sign Error
stories.one_liner: OpenAI withdrew three mathematics papers and revised 14 other manuscripts after a sign error invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument.
stories.summary: On October 7, 2026, OpenAI withdrew three math manuscripts because a sign error in the paper on Weil classes invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and the construction used by two dependent papers. The withdrawn papers are Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds, Algebraicity of Kuga-Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces, and The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces. OpenAI also revised 14 other manuscripts with proof repairs, corrected statements, and clearer hypotheses. Additionally, the team added 6 formalizations and 5 other additions, bringing the total percentage of top-line results formalized to 300 out of 719, or about 42 percent.
stories.eli5: OpenAI found a mistake in a math proof, like a wrong plus or minus sign, so they had to take back three math papers that relied on it. They also fixed some other papers to make sure the math is correct.
stories.why_it_matters: Mathematical proof errors require careful retraction and revision of dependent manuscripts to maintain the integrity of formal results.

stories.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
stories.one_liner: TokenRouter is a new serving system designed to efficiently handle token-level LLM routing in inference work.
stories.summary: Large language model routing distributes inference work across different models. Coarse-grained routing at the session or query level is common in production systems, but token-level routing offers efficiency and quality gains. Current systems face challenges like step desynchronization and batch admission delays under token-level routing. Researchers designed TokenRouter to solve these challenges. TokenRouter uses request-centric programming and model-centric execution. It launches a subserver for each LLM and dispatches requests asynchronously. Each subserver uses a delayed-batching scheduler. TokenRouter achieves 2.01-64.15x higher decoding throughput than existing systems across diverse routing algorithms, workloads, and model pairs.
stories.eli5: When you have two different AI helpers, TokenRouter is like a smart traffic cop that decides word by word which helper should write the next part.
stories.why_it_matters: Higher decoding throughput makes token-level routed large language model inference practical for production systems.

stories.title: Microsoft Introduces Microsoft-Decision-1 for Fast Decision-Scoring
stories.one_liner: Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a new model for fast decision-scoring designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control.
stories.summary: Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a decision-scoring model available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter. The model is built by post-training Qwen3.5-9B for single-pass decision scoring, and Microsoft plans to rebase it on other models including Microsoft AI and OpenAI. stories.title: SparseDecoding Proposes Decoding-Aware Pruning for LLM Inference
stories.one_liner: SparseDecoding is a decoding-aware pruning framework designed to improve accurate and efficient large language model inference.
stories.summary: Large language model inference suffers from significant latency during the decoding stage because of its memory-bound nature. Layer-wise training-free network pruning guided by the Hessian is a known solution, but typical methods compute the Hessian using pre-collected natural sequences. This creates a distribution shift from self-generated tokens. SparseDecoding addresses this by constructing calibration matrices from layer-wise activations collected during dense-model autoregressive generation, excluding prefill. This aligns the pruning objective with decoding activations.
stories.eli5: Pruning a language model is like trimming unneeded branches off a tree to make it lighter, and SparseDecoding makes sure you trim the right parts by watching how the tree actually grows.
stories.why_it_matters: Aligning pruning objectives with actual decoding activations reduces performance loss during efficient large language model inference.

new_terms.definition: A principled pruning framework tailored for accurate and efficient LLM decoding by aligning the pruning objective with decoding activations.

stories.title: Researchers Present Opera Verbal Critic Framework for Coding Agents
stories.one_liner: Opera is a verbal critic framework that treats corrections as persistent notes to improve long-horizon coding agents.
stories.summary: Long-horizon coding agents need timely corrections, but feedback often misjudges work or misses underlying problems. Researchers present Opera, a verbal critic framework that treats each correction as a persistent note until the diagnosed problem is resolved. Opera decides when to review through periodic and event-driven triggers, diagnoses issues with typed operators, audits feedback against visible evidence, and tracks subsequent actions. As a test-time critic, Opera improves resolve rates on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1. Opera-guided rollouts also provide on-policy training data to fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B.
stories.eli5: Coding agents sometimes need someone to check their work, so this new tool acts like a careful coach that writes down notes and checks back later to see if the computer actually fixed the bug.
stories.why_it_matters: Using a persistent verbal critic framework during test time and for rollouts improves resolve rates for coding agents.

new_terms.definition: A framework that treats each correction as a persistent note, followed until the diagnosed problem is resolved.
